routine.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/view → resources[].kind + priority + createdAt · 899 routine arrivals with a patientId, created inside a 9.27 sim-day window, divided by that window
routine.note: Two independent routes agree. Ours: 96.993 routine (GP site) + 43.576 urgent + 2.142 complex (hospital site) = 142.711/sim-day. Kaavya counted A&E attendances separately at ≈142/sim-day, σ ≈ 1.2 over nine sim-days. Different endpoints, different denominators, same total — this is the strongest evidence in the set, and it is what licenses treating total demand as fixed. Range is her [140, 144] band allocated to this class by its share of the total; no class-level band exists.

complex.citation: GET /api/sites/hospital/view → resources[].kind + priority + createdAt · 52 complex arrivals with a patientId, created inside a 24.28 sim-day window, divided by that window
complex.note: Counted, but under OUR definition: NHS-SIM has only acuity 2 and 3, so "complex" is our construct — demand whose pathway touches more than one service owner. The count is measured; the class boundary is a modelling choice and the split between complex and urgent moves with it. Kaavya's baseline carried 0 here because her A&E read cannot see multi-service pathways.

urgent.citation: GET /api/sites/hospital/view → resources[].kind + priority + createdAt · 1058 urgent arrivals with a patientId, created inside a 24.28 sim-day window, divided by that window
urgent.note: Disagrees with her baseline of 0.3/sim-day, and ours wins on method: hers counts acuity-2 A&E attendances only, n=3 across nine days, which is too thin to rate. Ours counts urgent-priority demand at the hospital site over the same window, n in the hundreds. Both are right about their own denominator; this one is the denominator the engine needs.

gpSessionsPerDay.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/appointments?date=2026-09-18 → sessions[] · 6 appointment sessions published for 2026-09-18
gpSessionsPerDay.note: Her table calls this measured; we tag it documented because the server publishes the session list rather than us watching six sessions happen. Same number, 6, either way.

gpSlotsPerSession.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/appointments?date=2026-09-18 → sessions[] · sum over 6 sessions of floor((endsAt - startsAt) / slotMinutes) minus blocked slots · divided by 6 published sessions
gpSlotsPerSession.note: Derived: usable slots/day ÷ sessions/day. Matches her 6 × (16 − 1) independently, which is the only cross-check we have on the protected break being counted once.

communitySlotsPerDay.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Capacities — capacity-community resource declares total: 4, remaining: 4
communitySlotsPerDay.note: Hers: our GP view holds no community capacity resource. The binding constraint, and the best lever we have — the base is 4, so the multiplier bites hard and thresholds are visible. No range: the server declares one integer, and a spread here would be invented. The capacity multiplier lever carries the policy spread instead.

staffedSpaces.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Capacities — view.staffing — 4 doctors + 4 nurses = 8 staffed spaces
staffedSpaces.note: Hers: staffing is not in the GP site view we read. No range — a staffing establishment is a count, not an estimate.

gpAdminShare.note: ⚠️ UNSOURCED. Her baseline tags this literature, but the corpus index (corpus/sources.md) is still empty, so there is no citation to render and literature would be a claim we cannot back. Assumed and amber until Albert indexes a source. It couples the clinic and admin queues, so expect the tornado to rank it high — a dominant parameter with neither a citation nor a range is exactly the case PRD §8.5 asks to be raised, not smoothed over.

gpConsultation.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/appointments?date=2026-09-18 → sessions[] · commonest slotMinutes across 6 published sessions
gpConsultation.note: This is the published slot length, not an observed consultation. It cannot be observed: 1,307 of 1,312 attendances are still waiting, so nothing has been served to time. Treat it as the scheduled service time the rota implies.

communityVisit.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Service times — provenance.changes, schedule_visit → visit.completed, n=7
communityVisit.note: Constant in the ground truth: measured variance is exactly zero across every observed transition. No range — a spread here would contradict the simulator rather than describe uncertainty about it. If the engine draws this from a distribution, that is a deliberate divergence and must be declared. Also matches the handbook figure exactly, which is what upgraded it from documented to measured.

documentReviewHop.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Service times — provenance.changes on discharge-summary — sent→reviewed n=20, reviewed→filed n=8
documentReviewHop.note: Constant in the ground truth: measured variance is exactly zero across every observed transition. No range — a spread here would contradict the simulator rather than describe uncertainty about it. If the engine draws this from a distribution, that is a deliberate divergence and must be declared.

bloodResultTurnaround.note: Not yet observed live — this world has no completed result transitions, a consequence of the same gridlock. No range: the handbook states a single figure.

pharmacyApproval.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/view → resources[].dueAt - createdAt where kind = prescription · median dueAt - createdAt over 7 prescription resources (identical across every observation); server-set due window, not an observed service time
pharmacyApproval.note: Disagrees with her baseline of 60 min, and neither number is an observed duration. Hers is a bare assumption; ours is the due window the server stamps on every prescription (n=7, identical every time) — the SLA it promises, not the time work took. Exactly one approved prescription exists in the world, so the real service time is not measurable. Point estimate at the declared window, with her 60 as the optimistic end of the range: that spread is the genuine uncertainty here.

gpToTest.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/view → resources[].owner ordered by patientId + createdAt · 7 of 12 observed handoffs out of gp, from per-patient resource timelines
gpToTest.note: Ours, and it overturns her baseline of 0.2 by a wide margin. `diagnostics` is the owner behind the test node, and it takes most of what leaves the GP. n=12 handoffs, so the Wilson interval is wide — carry it rather than the point estimate, because a share this dominant with a thin n is precisely where the three worlds should separate.

gpToHospital.note: ⚠️ Not measured. None of the 12 observed handoffs out of the GP owner went to a hospital or referrals owner; they went to diagnostics, triage and messaging. The point estimate is Kaavya's baseline assumption. The range is what 0 of 12 genuinely supports as an upper bound, so the sampler is constrained by evidence even where the centre is not.

gpToCommunity.note: ⚠️ Not measured. None of the 12 observed handoffs out of the GP owner went to the community owner; they went to diagnostics, triage and messaging. The point estimate is Kaavya's baseline assumption. The range is what 0 of 12 genuinely supports as an upper bound, so the sampler is constrained by evidence even where the centre is not. The only 7 community visits in the world were created by team14 via schedule_visit, so there is no baseline referral flow anywhere in the sim to measure this from.

letterSentToReviewed.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · The discharge funnel — 21 of 57 letters that reached the GP progressed past sent
letterSentToReviewed.note: Hers: the discharge funnel is not visible in the GP site view we page. Real attrition, n=57, and the best routing evidence anyone on the team has.

letterReviewedToFiled.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · The discharge funnel — 9 of 57 letters reached filed
letterReviewedToFiled.note: Hers. Unconditional on review, as her contract defines it: 9 of all 57 sent, not 9 of the 12 reviewed. 84% of letters are never filed — the manual chasing Chapter 3 is about.

communityRejection.note: Community refuses at capacity with a 409 — we have provoked one — but there is no baseline referral flow to measure how often it happens, so the rate is undeclarable. No range: we would be inventing both ends.

communityCapacityMultiplier.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Recommendations per lever — community capacity × 4 slots/day, grounded
communityCapacityMultiplier.note: Baseline = no policy applied, so this sits at the identity. Extraction moves it from the uploaded document and the slider moves it afterwards; no range, because a lever's spread is a policy choice, not uncertainty for the three-worlds sampler. The base it scales is 4 slots/day, which is what makes this the best lever we have: small base, visible thresholds.

extraGpSessions.citation: GET /api/sites/gp/appointments?date=2026-09-18 → sessions[] · 6 appointment sessions published for 2026-09-18 · baseline additional sessions
extraGpSessions.note: Baseline = no policy applied, so this sits at the identity. Extraction moves it from the uploaded document and the slider moves it afterwards; no range, because a lever's spread is a policy choice, not uncertainty for the three-worlds sampler. One extra session = +15 slots ≈ +17%.

telephoneFollowUpShare.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Recommendations per lever — 2 of 6 sessions have data.mode = telephone
telephoneFollowUpShare.note: Hers: session mode is not in the view payload we page. n=6 sessions, so the interval is genuinely wide — that width is the evidence, not a modelling choice.

monitoringIntensity.citation: docs/calibration-findings.md · Recommendations per lever — devices active, 484 observations available
monitoringIntensity.note: Baseline = no policy applied, so this sits at the identity. Extraction moves it from the uploaded document and the slider moves it afterwards; no range, because a lever's spread is a policy choice, not uncertainty for the three-worlds sampler. The BASE is measured; the EFFECT of monitoring on admission is not in the sim at all and must come from the corpus before any finding rests on this lever.

hospitalToCommunityShare.note: ⚠️ NOT GROUNDED — do not present as measured. There is no baseline hospital→community flow anywhere in NHS-SIM; the only 7 community visits were created by team14. Her contract asks for `literature`, and it becomes literature the moment Albert indexes a source, but corpus/sources.md is empty today and literature without a citation would be a claim we cannot produce. Assumed and amber until then. The discharge funnel (routing.letterSentToReviewed) is the closest proxy we have.

weekdayDischargeShare.note: ⚠️ NOT GROUNDED — do not present as measured. NHS-SIM has no weekday logic at all: sessions are seeded for a fixed 7-day window from world creation, so Sat 12th has 6 sessions and Sat 19th has 0. The value 1 means "no weekday shaping", which is the only thing the ground truth can represent. Amber on screen. No range: there is nothing to spread between.

inducedDemand.note: Declared at 0, not defaulted to 0. NHS-SIM generates ~142 arrivals/sim-day regardless of what anyone does, so Roemer-style induced demand cannot occur in the ground truth: freed capacity has nothing to refill it with. Report the reverse breakeven — "induced demand would have to exceed X% to overturn this" — which is a stronger answer than a fitted number.

substitution.note: Declared at 0, not defaulted to 0. NHS-SIM generates ~142 arrivals/sim-day regardless of what anyone does, so the bottleneck cannot relocate: demand is exogenous and fixed. Report the breakeven.

gaming.note: Declared at 0, not defaulted to 0. NHS-SIM generates ~142 arrivals/sim-day regardless of what anyone does, so there is nothing to game — the sim has no coding, no reclassification and no target to hit. Report the breakeven.
